s.n: Valjean's loaf with salted butter and radishes
s.note: A crackling, dark-crusted country loaf torn at the table, with salted butter, crisp radishes and salt flakes
s.how: Mix 500g bread flour, 7g dried yeast, 10g salt and 400ml warm water to a sticky dough and cover for 2 hours until doubled. Tip onto a floured bench, fold the edges in to make a round and set seam side down on floured baking paper. Heat the oven to 240C with a lidded cast iron pot inside for 30 minutes. Lift the loaf on its paper into the pot, slash the top and bake for 25 minutes with the lid on, then 15 minutes with it off, until dark and crusty. Cool for 30 minutes, then tear and serve with 125g soft salted butter, a bunch of trimmed radishes and salt flakes.

s.note: Pork belly slow-cooked with garlic and thyme until it falls apart, shredded into its own fat, with toasted baguette, cornichons and mustard
s.how: Heat the oven to 150C. Toss 800g cubed pork belly with 2 tsp salt and 1 tsp black pepper in a small lidded casserole with 4 garlic cloves, 2 bay leaves, 4 thyme sprigs and 200ml water. Cover and cook for 3 hours until the meat falls apart. Pick out the herbs, shred the pork and garlic with two forks and work in enough of the fat to make it soft. Pack into jars, pour the rest of the fat over and chill for 2 hours until set. Serve at room temperature with toasted baguette, cornichons and Dijon mustard.

m.note: Chicken thighs braised in red wine with smoky bacon, eschalots, mushrooms and thyme, with buttery boiled potatoes
m.how: Fry 150g smoked bacon lardons in a large casserole until crisp and lift out. Season 1.5kg bone-in chicken thighs and brown well in the fat, then lift out. Brown 12 peeled eschalots and 250g button mushrooms in the pot. Stir in 2 crushed garlic cloves and 2 tbsp plain flour, then 750ml red wine, 250ml chicken stock, 2 bay leaves and 4 thyme sprigs. Return the chicken and bacon, cover and simmer gently for 1 hour, then uncover and simmer for 15 minutes until the sauce coats a spoon. Meanwhile boil 800g small waxy potatoes. Stir 30g butter into the sauce, scatter with parsley and serve with the potatoes.

w.n: Little Cosette's winter pears with chocolate sauce
w.note: Whole pears poached in vanilla, cinnamon and orange syrup, with a warm dark chocolate sauce
w.how: Simmer 1 litre of water, 200g caster sugar, 1 tsp vanilla, 1 cinnamon stick and 3 strips of orange peel in a pan that fits the pears snugly. Add 4 peeled firm pears with their stalks on, cover with a circle of baking paper and poach gently for 25 minutes, turning now and then, until tender. Cool in the syrup for 30 minutes. Heat 125ml thickened cream until steaming, pour over 100g chopped dark chocolate and stir until smooth. Serve each pear standing in a little syrup with the warm chocolate sauce poured over.

d.note: Red wine warmed with honey, orange, cinnamon, clove and star anise, served steaming in glasses
d.how: Put 750ml red wine, 250ml water, 80g honey, 1 sliced orange, 2 cinnamon sticks, 6 cloves and 2 star anise in a saucepan and warm over low heat for 12 minutes, stirring until the honey melts. Do not let it boil. Take off the heat and steep for 10 minutes, then ladle into 4 heatproof glasses with a slice of orange in each.
